long_biography.plain_text:
Gavio entered the industrial network created by his father Marcellino and uncle Pietro, whose freight, construction and toll-road interests became one of Italy's major infrastructure groups. After both men died in 2009, Beniamino and other second-generation family members assumed ownership and leadership responsibilities. He became chairman of Aurelia, the family's principal holding company, and of Nuova Argo, the vehicle through which Aurelia and outside investor Ardian control ASTM.

His tenure has been active rather than custodial. The group moved further into international concessions, including the acquisition of a strategic Brazilian platform, and brought institutional capital into the ownership structure while retaining family control. Gavio now sits on ASTM's board and chairs the two holding companies above it. He inherited the core wealth-producing asset but also helped expand and reorganise it, supporting Inherited and expanded as the origin and Operator as his relationship. Aurelia's family ownership and his documented direct stakes establish personal economic participation; they do not make ASTM's roads, construction contracts, debt, revenue or transaction values his personal assets.
